oracles.assertion: As a QWork platform administrator, I want to add a Provider URL and credential, so that platform models can use a centrally managed upstream service.
As a QWork platform administrator, I want Provider credentials to be write-only and encrypted, so that secrets cannot be read back from APIs or logs.
As a QWork platform administrator, I want to rotate a credential without changing the public model identity, so that key rotation does not break saved sessions or billing history.
As a QWork platform administrator, I want to test Provider connectivity before publication, so that obvious endpoint, authentication and protocol mistakes are caught safely.
As a security reviewer, I want Provider endpoints restricted to public HTTPS by default, so that the model gateway cannot be used for SSRF or internal-network discovery.
As an operations reviewer, I want private Provider access to require an explicit allowlist, so that internal egress remains separately approved and auditable.
As a QWork platform administrator, I want to declare context and output limits, so that ZiqDo and the real Provider request share the same budgets.

As a QWork platform administrator, I want to configure default and enforced Provider parameters while exposing no arbitrary client override, so that logged-in users can adjust only the published reasoning effort choices.
As a QWork platform administrator, I want one active Provider Route per model in the first release, so that routing and cost attribution remain deterministic.
As a QWork platform administrator, I want invalid references and unsupported parameters rejected before publication, so that an incomplete version cannot become active.
As a QWork platform administrator, I want publication to create an immutable version, so that every request and charge can be explained later.
As a QWork platform administrator, I want to republish a previous configuration as a new revision, so that rollback is explicit and auditable.
As an operator, I want qwork_server to load a valid published revision without restart, so that routine model changes do not require a service rollout.
As an operator, I want a failed new revision to leave the last validated revision active, so that bad configuration does not silently stop all model traffic.
As a logged-in QWork user, I want to see only models distributed by the current published catalog, so that the selector reflects the platform’s actual offering.
As a logged-in QWork user, I want a selected model to retain its stable identity across route changes, so that existing sessions and usage history remain understandable.
As a logged-in QWork user, I want to choose only reasoning efforts supported by the selected model, so that the displayed choice has real effect.
As a logged-in QWork user, I want fixed-effort models to omit the effort selector, so that the UI does not promise unsupported control.
As a logged-in QWork user, I want my last valid effort choice remembered per model on this device, so that model switching remains convenient without uploading preferences.
As a logged-in QWork user, I want unsupported cached effort values to fall back to the published default, so that catalog changes do not create invalid requests.
As a QWork platform administrator, I want canonical effort values translated by the Provider Route, so that different upstream protocols receive the fields they actually support.
As a logged-in QWork user, I want Max mode to preserve emergency context protection, so that long sessions still recover before an unrecoverable overflow.
As a logged-in QWork user, I want Max mode stored only on my device, so that a context preference does not become cloud profile data.
As a logged-in QWork user, I want Max mode billed by actual token usage without a separate multiplier, so that Credits reflect real consumption.

As a QWork platform administrator, I want catalog visibility and serving status to be independent controls, so that a model can be withdrawn from discovery without abruptly stopping existing sessions.
As a logged-in QWork user, I want a serving-disabled model to reject the next not-yet-started call clearly, so that failures are deterministic rather than silently rerouted.
As a logged-in QWork user, I want an in-flight request to finish with its starting configuration and price snapshot, so that publication or shutdown changes cannot alter an active charge.
As a finance operator, I want supplier cost tied to the actual Provider Route and user Credits tied to the public model and published version, so that margin and user pricing can both be audited.
As a QWork user with a local custom model, I want my endpoint, Key and usage to remain local, so that the platform control plane does not absorb BYOK data.
As an Ollama user, I want local discovery and calls to remain outside the platform catalog and billing, so that local inference remains private.
As a release reviewer, I want every initial model and effort tier probed against the real test Provider, so that published mappings are based on evidence rather than model-name assumptions.
As a maintainer, I want old clients to have an explicit compatibility result, so that the V2 rollout does not produce ambiguous parameter drift.
As a maintainer, I want legacy platform-model tables removed only after all consumers migrate, so that the expand–contract transition remains green and reversible.
